summary.prose: Building s3 means adding the reconciliation pass to src/workflow/review-round/: a fixed four-verdict taxonomy, the ReconciliationResult shape, and reconcileRound itself -- a dedicated classification call that compares a prior round's HIGH/MED findings against the current round's findings, reading the review's temp-folder audit trail internally only if the two finding sets alone don't resolve a verdict. The internal classification and audit-trail read are made testable through a module-level test-injection seam, matching the codebase's existing convention, so the full test suite runs without a live LLM call or real filesystem fixture.

tasks.title: Add ReconciliationVerdict, ReconciliationResult and reconcileRound
tasks.summary: Add src/workflow/review-round/reconciliation.ts exporting ReconciliationVerdict (fixed 4-member union), ReconciliationResult {priorFindingRef, verdict} (sc3's interfaceSketch), and reconcileRound(reviewId, priorFindings, currentFindings) which makes one dedicated classification call per prior finding set, reading .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ internally only when needed. Includes a module-level _setReconciliationDepsForTests seam (matching src/workflow/team/signoff.ts's convention) injecting the classification call and the audit-trail read, defaulting to the real CliProvider-backed implementation, plus a compile-time typecheck fixture.
acceptanceChecks: ReconciliationVerdict, ReconciliationResult and reconcileRound are exported exactly as dataModelChanges/contractDetails specify, with no extra or missing field or parameter
reconcileRound never performs its own re-grounding pass and never folds reconciliation into the same pass that produced currentFindings
the typecheck fixture rejects an invalid verdict literal and an added/removed ReconciliationResult key via @ts-expect-error / Equal<keyof ReconciliationResult,...>
a rejecting classification call propagates its rejection unchanged rather than returning partial or fabricated results

tests.name: reconcileRound produces exactly one ReconciliationResult per entry in priorFindings, keyed by that finding's own id

tasks.title: Add the full named test suite for reconcileRound/ReconciliationResult
tasks.summary: One it() per testStrategy.testLevels subject (8 total) in __tests__/reconciliation.test.ts, matching ac1/ac2's acceptanceMapping.provingTests verbatim, using _setReconciliationDepsForTests to inject a spyable classification stub and a temp-directory fixture standing in for .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/.
acceptanceChecks: All 8 named test subjects from testStrategy.testLevels[0].subjects exist as individual it() cases with matching titles
ac1 and ac2's acceptanceMapping.provingTests all pass
npx tsx --test for the new test file passes with zero failures

tests.name: reconcileRound's parameters are reviewId and the two finding sets only -- no ReviewTargets-shaped parameter exists anywhere in its signature, so no re-grounding input is even possible
ReconciliationResult's exported shape contains exactly priorFindingRef and verdict, with no severity, blocking, or gate-facing field of any kind
ReconciliationVerdict accepts exactly the four fixed verdicts (confirmed, still-open, contradicted, no-longer-surfaced) and rejects any other value at compile time
a rejecting reconcileRound call propagates its rejection rather than returning partial or fabricated results
priorFindings as an empty array returns an empty array, not an error
two priorFindings entries with identical category and severity but different id values still produce two separate ReconciliationResult entries, keyed by their distinct ids

when the two finding sets alone do not resolve a classification, reconcileRound reads the audit trail itself from .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/, rather than requiring the caller to have pre-extracted and passed it in
